finding.before: The exact Fraction evaluator binds unary minus before exponentiation (-2^2 becomes4) and approximates irrational square roots as rational fractions. Historical exactness tests used floating tolerances and therefore did not establish exactness.
finding.after: Exponentiation binds before unary signs. Square-root output is a Fraction only when the reduced numerator and denominator are both exact squares; otherwise the API explicitly raises UnsupportedExpression. Existing rational tests now compare Fraction equality; all four former irrational cases remain tested as refusals.

scientific_argument: Unary negation in -a^2 applies to a^2 unless parentheses group the negative base. A reduced nonnegative rational p/q has a rational square root exactly when p and q are integer squares; isqrt plus equality of the squared roots verifies this condition without approximation.

tests.scope: Controlled arithmetic and variance-detection fixtures only; four tests reading/executing the real corpus were not run.

open_scientific_debts.reason: Unreadable options are assigned false without semantic proof.
Second-derivative-only classification can omit a degenerate extremum when other nondegenerate extrema coexist.
Automatic simplification such as x^3/x to x^2 can lose the original exclusion x!=0.

open_scientific_debts.controlled_evidence: With the exact Fraction API, V(X)=4 and sigma(X)=sqrt(3) produces no finding because the irrational claimed sigma is discarded as unreadable.
open_scientific_debts.impact: No zero-defect claim is supported by this consumer until unsupported claims remain explicitly visible.

not_run: Global QCM replay/generation until the listed scientific debts and dependent consumer are addressed.

independent_counterreview.read_scope: Entire Fraction parser, both test files, complete functional diff and all controlled cases executed.
independent_counterreview.scientific_reasoning: For a reduced p/q>=0, any rational square root m/n in lowest terms forces p=m² and q=n² by uniqueness of reduced fractions. Thus integer square roots followed by exact squaring tests are necessary and sufficient; no floating conversion is used. The unary production applies its sign after reading a power, while parentheses supply a signed base.
